faq.q: What is the gas that makes you cry?
faq.a: It is called syn-propanethial-S-oxide, sometimes called the tear factor. It irritates nerves in the eye and makes your eyes water.

faq.q: Why does cutting an onion release the gas?
faq.a: The enzymes and the sulfur chemicals sit in different parts of the onion's cells. Cutting breaks the cells, mixes them, and the gas forms within seconds.
asks: Why don't whole onions make you cry?

faq.q: How can you stop onions making you cry?
faq.a: Chill the onion first, use a sharp knife that crushes fewer cells, cut the root end last, and work near a fan or open window.
asks: Tips for cutting onions without tears

faq.q: Why don't cooked onions make you cry?
faq.a: Heat destroys the enzymes that make the gas, so cooked onions cannot produce it. That is also why cooked onions taste sweeter and milder.
asks: Why are fried onions not stinging?

faq.q: Why do onions have this chemical?
faq.a: It is a defence. Animals or insects that bite into an onion get a sharp, stinging blast, which puts them off eating it.
asks: Why do onions make tear gas?

facts: The irritant gas from cut onions is called syn-propanethial-S-oxide.
In 2002 Japanese scientists discovered that a separate enzyme, lachrymatory factor synthase, is needed to make the tear gas.
